links.why: cl2 is a wayyiqtol (fused waw) and continues the narrative line; the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech is cl0, since cl1 is God's quoted speech.
links.category: narrative line skipping an embedded speech

links.why: cl1 is the jussive inside the quoted speech and is not on the narrative line, so cl2 does not follow it as a next event; the relation between them is carried out, which is a fulfilment, not a sequence.
links.category: speech clause treated as narrative step

links.why: cl0 is the speech clause 'God said' and cl1 is what was said, embedded in the speaking.

cl2 'and there was light' repeats the verb of the jussive 'let there be light' and reports that the word was carried out; the ken pro-form of the fulfilment rule is absent, so this is by repeated verb and the sense, and is flagged in none_fit.
links.category: fulfilment of an earlier command by repeated verb

groups.why: cl0 'God said' introduces the speech, cl1 is what is said, and the subject of the saying is God (w2). No addressee is named in the verse.
groups.category: speech turn without a stated addressee

groups.why: cl1 is the command (jussive). 'part' is not a role of the imperative group, and cl2 is a wayyiqtol narrative report, not a waw plus third-person weqatal, so it is not the group's effect.
groups.category: report of carrying out wrongly placed inside the command group

groups.why: A command (cl1) followed by the same act reported as having happened (cl2, 'there was light', repeating the verb).
groups.category: command and the same act reported as done

none_fit.what: The fulfilment rule asks for a pro-form (ken); this verse has none, only the repeated verb 'was', so the fulfils link rests on the repeated verb and the sense. A form for a report of carrying out by repeating the command's verb, without ken, is not among the link types.

cant_tell.why: The verse names no one God speaks to, so the turn has no addressee member.
